segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Yeah, so Northstar Plastics is still good for 46 seats, annual, net 30. Total is $41,860 before tax, and they want the June 3 go-live called out in the order form.

segments.speaker: Mark
segments.text: Okay. Is the buyer changing anything, or are we just waiting on our side?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Buyer is fine. Procurement approved the 12-month term yesterday. Legal still owns the indemnity cap line; I put a fresh note in that thread after lunch, so the order form is staying as a draft for now.

segments.speaker: Mark
segments.text: Got it. The cap was two times fees, right?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Right, and their paper asked for uncapped. We already got them down to two times in email, just need our yes on the wording.

segments.speaker: Mark
segments.text: Discount is within the pricing sheet at that seat count, so no issue there.

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: Yeah. The only pricing wrinkle is the co-term for the five add-on seats in September. Deal desk has my 9:30 comment with the math, and the e-sign packet is waiting on that final total.

segments.speaker: Mark
segments.text: Makes sense. If they ask today, tell them we’re targeting signature by Friday?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: I already told Emily Friday is realistic if the final packet lands by tomorrow afternoon. Implementation can still hold the kickoff for May 28.

segments.speaker: Mark
segments.text: Any security items left from their questionnaire?

segments.speaker: Dana
segments.text: One line. Encryption at rest for backups. Security has the draft answer with my note under it, and once they fill that in I can send the complete response back to Emily.

segments.speaker: Mark
segments.text: Okay, keep the customer warm with the timeline, but don’t send partials. Sounds close.
